description: Design a data structure that supports adding points on a 2D plane and counting the number of axis-aligned squares that can be formed with a given query point as one corner.
intuition: For each query point, fix one side of the square along the same row. The side length determines exactly where to look for the other two corners. Multiplying point counts handles duplicates correctly.
approach: Store point counts in a hash map. For a query point (qx, qy), iterate over all points (px, qy) on the same y-coordinate. For each, the side length is |px - qx|, then check if (qx, qy +/- side) and (px, qy +/- side) exist.
explanation:
1. Store count of each point and a map from y-coordinate to list of x-coordinates.
2. For query (qx, qy), find all points (px, qy) on the same row.
3. The side length is |px - qx|. Check above and below for the other two corners.
4. Multiply counts of the three other corners (handling duplicates).
5. Sum all valid squares.
timeComplexity: Constructor: O(1); add: O(1); count: O(R + 1)
hints: Fix one side of the square along the same y-coordinate as the query point.
The side length determines where to look for the other two corners.
Use point counts to handle duplicate points correctly.
